resources.name: Molecular structures of n-butanol, ethanol, and gasoline surrogate components

access.notes: SMILES or 2D/3D structures can be obtained from PubChem or common chemical databases.

resources.notes: Includes n-butanol, ethanol, and the gasoline surrogate molecules listed in Burri et al. Table 1 (isooctane, n-heptane, toluene, 2-methylbutane, m-xylene, 2,2,4-trimethylpentane, 2-methylpentane, n-butane, 1,2,4-trimethylbenzene, n-pentane, 2,3,4-trimethylpentane, 2,2,3-trimethylpentane, 3-methylpentane, o-xylene, ethylbenzene, benzene, p-xylene, 2,3-dimethylbutane, n-hexane, 1-methyl-3-ethylbenzene, 1-methyl-4-ethylbenzene, 3-methylhexane, 2-methylhexane).

resources.name: Gasoline surrogate composition (Burri et al. 2004)

access.notes: Table 1 in Burri et al. lists weight percentages for regular gasoline components. The composition is needed to compute mole fractions for blending.

resources.notes: The exact weight fractions from Burri et al. Fuel 83 (2004) 187-193, Table 1 must be used to define the G100 blend.

resources.name: NIST experimental Cp for gas-phase n-butanol at 298.15 K

access.notes: The NIST Chemistry WebBook entry for n-butanol provides the experimental constant-pressure heat capacity value.

resources.notes: Used as the reference for Cp validation.

resources.name: Open-source DFT software (ORCA or PySCF)

access.notes: Any DFT code supporting B3LYP with the 6-311++G(d,p) basis set and thermochemistry analysis is acceptable.

resources.notes: The open-source code replaces the paper's proprietary Gaussian09W.
